title: Recovering from a Failed Reforestation Attempt
paragraphs: After a well-funded reforestation project in his region failed to establish more than a small fraction of planted saplings, Wira was assigned to investigate what had gone wrong before attempting a second, better-informed effort.

His investigation revealed that the original project had used a single tree species uniformly across the entire area, ignoring significant variation in soil quality and moisture levels across different sections of land.

Rather than repeating the same broad approach with minor adjustments, Wira proposed a more labor-intensive method matching specific tree species to the particular conditions of each individual section of the reforestation site.

Though considerably more complex to implement, this tailored approach produced survival rates nearly three times higher than the original attempt, teaching Wira that respecting local variation mattered more than convenient uniformity.
